attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway for the private "lan" network (10.50.50.0/24, egress:false) so node2 and node3 can reach the internet through it, implemented via an idempotent Ansible playbook run from control_node node4. node1's eth1 got a static LAN address plus a source-NAT masquerade rule outbound on eth0; node2/node3's enp8s0 got static LAN IPs plus source-based policy routing (ip rule + custom table 200 via NetworkManager) so traffic sourced from their private LAN address routes through node1, while their separate mgmt-network default route (used for cluster/exec connectivity) is left untouched. Verified via ping/curl from the LAN addresses and conntrack/nft masquerade counters on node1. Also fixed a VyOS SSH-key persistence issue (authorized_keys is regenerated from declarative config on boot) by adding the ansible key via `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys`. All four nodes were restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot_id changes were captured for each and NAT/routing/connectivity were reverified as fully recovered and persistent after every restart, with a final idempotent (all-ok, zero-changed) Ansible run confirming durable configuration.
